items.headline: Update: Six charged over unpermitted assemblies, including Kirsten Han and actors Lim Kay Siu and Neo Swee Lin
items.summary: Six people aged 31 to 70 were charged on Sep 28 over public assemblies held without a permit outside the State Courts and near Changi Prison. They include freelance journalist and activist Kirsten Han, 37, and actor couple Lim Kay Siu, 70, and Neo Swee Lin, 63; the charges follow earlier prosecutions tied to the same anti-death-penalty gatherings.

items.headline: Man, 69, convicted of breaching a protection order by singing and banging cans outside a neighbour's flat
items.summary: Heng Choo Hwi, 69, was convicted on Sep 28 after a trial over breaching a protection order. The court heard he sang and struck metal objects outside his neighbours' Housing Board flat, with a neighbour calling police at about 5:35pm on Feb 5.

items.headline: Man, 30, to be charged after allegedly faking an AI crocodile photo that shut Pandan Reservoir
items.summary: Police said a 30-year-old man will be charged on Sep 29 with transmitting a false message and obstructing the course of justice, after allegedly creating an AI-generated image of a crocodile at Pandan Reservoir and sending it to a colleague, prompting a suspension of activities before he deleted it.

items.headline: Woman, 54, jailed for paying S$52,900 in bribes to a former SJI facilities manager
items.summary: A 54-year-old Singaporean woman was sentenced on Sep 23 to three months and two weeks' jail after pleading guilty to paying more than S$52,000 in bribes to Ng Cher Him, a former St Joseph's Institution facilities manager, to secure maintenance work; Ng was jailed last year for taking bribes from several vendors.

items.headline: Update: North India and Nepal flood toll passes 100 as Uttar Pradesh deaths reach 81
items.summary: Days of intense rain have now killed more than 100 people across India and Nepal, with at least 81 dead in Uttar Pradesh. India's Central Water Commission said 30 river-monitoring stations across seven states were in a 'severe situation', with the Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Bagmati and Narmada above danger levels.

items.headline: Indian equities extend their slide to a seventh session as NSE shares fall below IPO price
items.summary: Indian stocks fell again on Sep 28 amid a broad equity selloff driven by costlier crude, a weaker rupee and foreign outflows. Shares of the National Stock Exchange of India slipped below their initial public offering price on their third day of trading, extending a lacklustre debut.

items.headline: Adani group firms settle a SEBI probe over public-shareholding rules
items.summary: Four Gautam Adani group firms - Adani Transmission, Adani Power, Adani Enterprises and Adani Ports - along with 14 directors, paid about 14.8 million rupees to settle a Securities and Exchange Board of India case over alleged breaches of minimum public-shareholding rules, resolving another regulatory matter for the conglomerate.

items.headline: India's trade minister Piyush Goyal heads to the US to push an interim trade pact
items.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal began a seven-day US trip on Sep 28, with finalising an interim trade agreement reached earlier this year topping his agenda alongside meetings with G20 counterparts; India has said a deal hinges on a preferential tariff rate for its exporters.

items.headline: Update: Healey pledges a 'new age of industrialisation' and puts fiscal discipline at the heart of the Budget
items.summary: In his Labour conference speech on Sep 28, Chancellor John Healey promised Britain a 'new age of industrialisation' and said fiscal discipline would be central to his first Budget on Oct 28, telling delegates he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham are 'united in meeting the fiscal rules'.

items.headline: Update: Burnham sets out a social care plan and refuses to rule out tax rises
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham used the Labour conference to detail plans for social care run 'on NHS principles' and free at the point of use, alongside water-sector reform and a focus on youth unemployment. Asked how he would fund it, he said 'nothing is off the table at this moment in time'.

items.headline: UK housebuilders jump as the government moves to revive a Help to Buy scheme
items.summary: London-listed housebuilders rallied on Sep 28 amid reports the Burnham government will reboot a Help to Buy-style scheme to support home ownership, with the FTSE 100 in focus as Chancellor John Healey addressed the Labour conference and markets weighed the looming Budget.

items.headline: City executives voice tax fears as Burnham courts small business at the conference
items.summary: Executives from big UK banks and professional-services firms privately voiced unease about the Burnham government's plans after 'business day' events at the Labour conference, as the prime minister stressed support for small business ahead of an Oct 28 Budget widely expected to raise taxes.

items.headline: Oil surges after Trump rejects Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Brent crude rose more than 3% toward $108 a barrel on Sep 28 after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. Tehran's plan, floated at the UN, sought the release of frozen funds, an end to oil sanctions and a lifting of the US naval blockade.

items.headline: Serbia calls a snap election for Oct 25 as Vucic faces a sustained student revolt
items.summary: Serbia will hold early parliamentary elections on Oct 25 after months of student-led protests over alleged corruption and negligence. Aleksandar Vucic, who is seeking the prime minister's post, is betting the vote keeps him in power, though analysts say it may not defuse the crisis.

items.headline: Ben-Gvir leads hundreds of Israelis into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
items.summary: Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir joined hundreds of Israelis who entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied East Jerusalem under police protection on Sep 28; Al Jazeera reported about 900 people entered during the morning.

items.headline: Update: Russian strikes kill eight across Ukraine and injure dozens in Kharkiv
items.summary: Russian attacks killed at least eight people across Ukraine and injured dozens on Sep 28, including at least 22 hurt when a guided aerial bomb hit a Kharkiv apartment block and three killed, among them a 16-year-old, in Sumy. Zelenskyy said Russia had launched more than 2,200 drones, 1,630 aerial bombs and 38 missiles in the past week.

items.headline: Viral AI agent startup Instinct raises $1bn Series C at a $10bn valuation
items.summary: Instinct, the invite-only personal AI agent that launched in August, raised a $1 billion Series C at a $10 billion valuation - up from $350 million at $2.5 billion just weeks earlier - underscoring investor frenzy for agents that carry out real-world tasks.

items.headline: Update: AI inference provider Modal Labs nears a $750m round at a $15.75bn valuation
items.summary: Modal Labs, which helps businesses run AI models on GPUs, is closing a roughly $750 million round led by Accel at a $15.75 billion valuation - more than triple the $4.65 billion it reached four months ago - as demand for inference infrastructure surges.

items.headline: Modulate raises $25m for voice-AI models that flag deepfakes and abuse
items.summary: Boston-based Modulate raised $25 million, led by Future Ventures, for its suite of small voice models offering transcription, emotion analysis, deepfake and AI-music detection, and policy enforcement for voice agents in regulated industries.

items.headline: The AI boom takes over New York Climate Week
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that AI dominated New York Climate Week on Sep 28, with much of the strongest climate-tech deal value flowing to sectors tied to data-centre build-out - grid infrastructure, the built environment and dispatchable energy - even as some attendees bristled at AI's growing footprint.

items.headline: US stocks fall as the Iran oil shock lifts Treasury yields to fresh highs
items.summary: Wall Street slipped on Sep 28 as surging crude and US-Iran tensions pushed Treasury yields higher: the S&P 500 fell 0.77% to about 7,684, the Dow lost 0.67% and the Nasdaq shed 0.92%. Nvidia bucked the trend, rising nearly 1% after unveiling a fresh buyback authorisation.

items.headline: Gold tumbles more than 3% as costlier crude keeps rate-hike bets alive
items.summary: Spot gold fell more than 3% to below $4,160 an ounce on Sep 28, with silver, platinum and palladium also sliding, as the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz kept energy costs high and pressure on the Federal Reserve; the 10-year Treasury yield jumped to about 5.27%, a 19-year high.

items.headline: Update: Paramount lines up a record $44bn bond sale to fund the Warner Bros Discovery takeover
items.summary: Paramount Skydance drew enough demand to cover a roughly $44 billion bond sale to finance its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, offering yields as high as about 9%. The $12.4 billion-equivalent of junk bonds, the biggest high-yield offering on record, had drawn more than $23 billion in orders by Monday morning.

items.headline: Nvidia lifts its buyback plan to about $235bn with a fresh $150bn authorisation
items.summary: Nvidia said it authorised an additional $150 billion for share repurchases, taking its total buyback plan to about $235 billion; the chipmaker's stock rose nearly 1% on Sep 28, outperforming a broadly weaker market weighed down by the oil-driven selloff.

items.headline: 🏎️ Update: Norris apologises to Colapinto after calling for a race ban
items.summary: Lando Norris said he messaged Franco Colapinto to apologise for saying after the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that 'some drivers shouldn't be in Formula 1' and calling for a one-race ban. Colapinto had triggered a restart pile-up in Baku that also eliminated Pierre Gasly and Norris; the Alpine driver keeps a five-place grid penalty for the next round at Sepang.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads the title race by 81 points as Mercedes eye both crowns
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli, 20, holds an 81-point championship lead over Mercedes team-mate George Russell after the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with Mercedes also topping the constructors' standings. On current form the Italian could be crowned as early as next month's Singapore Grand Prix (Oct 9-11).

items.headline: 🎾 Update: Hurkacz beats Shapovalov to reach the Chengdu Open final
items.summary: Hubert Hurkacz edged Denis Shapovalov 6-7(8), 6-3, 6-3 to reach the Chengdu Open final, the 13th tour-level final of his career. He will meet second seed Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the title match.

items.headline: 🏏 Update: Rain sends India and Pakistan into the Asian Games cricket semi-finals
items.summary: Both men's cricket quarter-finals in Nisshin were abandoned without a ball bowled on Sep 28 as persistent rain and a damp outfield intervened, sending India (over Afghanistan) and Pakistan (over Hong Kong) through as the higher-ranked teams. India will face the winner of Sri Lanka v Nepal.

items.headline: Landmark brain-cell atlas maps the genetics of Alzheimer's and seven other disorders
items.summary: The PsychAD consortium published a single-cell atlas of the human prefrontal cortex built from more than 6.3 million nuclei across 1,494 brains, linking gene-activity patterns to Alzheimer's and seven other brain disorders - a resource for tracing how genetic risk hits specific cell types.

items.headline: The brain's fats are organised into 'lipizones' that reorganise during pregnancy
items.summary: A new Nature lipidomic atlas mapped the membrane-lipid architecture of the adult mouse brain at micrometre scale, revealing distinct territories dubbed 'lipizones' that partly mirror cell-type zones but also trace distant axon terminals - and shift during pregnancy.

items.headline: An AI model is enlisted to attack a 79-year-old geometry problem about 6D spheres
items.summary: Scientific American reported that mathematician Levent Alpoge used an internal version of Anthropic's AI, Claude, to tackle the 1947 Hopf problem - whether a six-dimensional sphere can carry a complex structure - posting a 100-plus-page purported proof that the answer is yes. The result has not yet been verified.

items.headline: Mongolian fossils reclassify zhelestids, reshuffling an early branch of the mammal tree
items.summary: Newly described Cretaceous fossils from Mongolia show that zhelestids were not early relatives of hoofed placental mammals but a dental variant within Zalambdalestoidea, according to a study in Nature that combines distinctive molars with zalambdalestid skull and limb traits.

fun_fact.headline: Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold (the Mpemba effect)
fun_fact.body: Under the right conditions, hot water can freeze faster than cold water — a counter-intuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. It is named after Erasto Mpemba, a Tanzanian schoolboy who in 1963 noticed that his hot ice-cream mix froze quicker than a cold one and, though initially mocked, went on to co-publish the finding in 1969. Scientists still debate exactly why it happens.
fun_fact.source: Royal Society of Chemistry; Encyclopaedia Britannica

puzzle.title: Trailing Zeros
puzzle.body: How many zeros does the number 100! (100 factorial, i.e. 1 × 2 × 3 × … × 100) end in when written out in full?
puzzle.approach: The zeros come from factors of 10, and every 10 is a 2 paired with a 5 — so just count the 5s.
puzzle.answer:
24.
A trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2 × 5, and among 1–100 there are always more 2s than 5s, so the count of 5s is the limiting factor.
Multiples of 5 contribute one 5 each: 100 ÷ 5 = 20.
Multiples of 25 (25, 50, 75, 100) contribute one extra 5 each: 100 ÷ 25 = 4.
125 > 100, so there are no further factors.
Total = 20 + 4 = 24 trailing zeros.

word_puzzle.title: Compound Interest
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into four groups of four. In each group, all four words attach to the same hidden word to form common compounds.

TAROT · FOOT · BRIEF · WORK
POST · BASE · PILLOW · WOOD
SCORE · ODD · STAIR · MAN
REPORT · EYE · BOOK · SIDE
word_puzzle.approach: Each group's four words all pair with the SAME hidden word to make everyday compounds (like BRIEF → briefcase). Find the four partner words.
word_puzzle.answer:
Four hidden partner words:

CASE — BRIEFcase, STAIRcase, BOOKcase, PILLOWcase
CARD — TAROT card, POST card, SCOREcard, REPORT card
FIRE — FIREwork, FIREman, FIREside, FIREwood
BALL — BASEball, FOOTball, EYEball, ODDball

Watch-out: BASE tempts 'base case', but baseball is the only fit that leaves every group with exactly four.
